title: Member Handbook: How Many Primary Care Provider Assignments a Member Holds
content:
A member of Prairie Ridge Health Plan holds a **Primary Care Provider Assignment** in their own name. This handbook section sets out how many of those assignments can be open for one member at a time.

## The rule

1. A member may hold **at most two** open Primary Care Provider Assignments at the same time: the current active assignment, and one pending-effective assignment that will replace it.
2. Assignments are never shared between members. Each household member holds their own Primary Care Provider Assignment, even where two household members see the same provider.

## The same rule, set out by holding

| What the member holds | Open assignments counted |
|---|---|
| One active assignment | 1 |
| One active assignment and one pending-effective assignment that will replace it | 2, the most a member may hold |
| A household member's assignment with the same provider | 0 — it belongs to the household member, not to this member |

## Points of judgement

- **Is a parent's assignment the child's assignment?** No. Each member holds their own; a child assigned to the same practice as a parent has a separate Primary Care Provider Assignment.
- **What is the most a member can have open?** Two: the active one and the one pending-effective assignment that will replace it.
- **Hypothetical example.** A member has an active assignment with one practice and a pending-effective assignment with another. That member holds two open assignments, which is the limit stated above.
